title: Book One · Chapter 107: The Place for the Work Shirt
story:
Dad asks Mum to mend the elbow of his work shirt.

Not tonight, he says. Any time before Monday will do. He has another shirt for the next two days.

Mum looks at the tear. She writes it on her list. She does not put aside a customer's coat to begin at once.

Ronan watches Dad hang the shirt on a peg by the toolbox. The peg is new. “Where can I put this peg?” Dad asked Mrs Lan. She agreed to this place by the toolbox.

“Will that be your work place now?” Ronan asks.

“The shirt's place?”

“Mr Sun's.”

Dad sits down to take off his shoes.

“Yes. We agreed regular work days for this year. The pay is still low. But now we know my work hours.”

Ronan likes the sound of regular. He thinks of Dad's work card. Dad knows his work days now. The shirt hangs ready for another week.

“Does he still check your work?”

“We check difficult work together. I check his written list sometimes too.”

“Do you tell him when it is wrong?”

“When I find something wrong.”

“Does he like it?”

Dad smiles a little. “Not always. Neither do I.”

Mum brings tea. Mum has news of her own. Two people brought her sewing jobs. They saw her pocket work on the dress. The owner told them about Mum's good repair. She remembered both the mistake and the good repair.

“Do you need a bigger table?” Ronan asks.

“I need you to take your folder off this one,” she says.

He moves it to the shelf. That solves today's table problem. Two new customers brought work. The family still needs to use this old table.

After supper, Dad shows them his new work notes. There are spaces for the job and the needed part. Another space is for the promised time. Mr Sun agreed to the page after Dad tried it for several weeks.

“Is that your idea?” Ronan asks.

“Some of it. We changed it together.”

Ronan wants the page beside the school book. Dad says he needs it at work. It may have customers' names on it too.

“Can I draw the empty boxes?”

“Yes. Leave the names out.”

He draws three plain boxes on a scrap. They look almost like his own test spaces. He knows the jobs inside are different.

Later, Mum tries Dad's shirt over her arm to find the tear. Mum asks for the dark cloth tin. Ronan fetches it. He does not choose a patch without her.

Dad takes the wooden boat from the shelf and checks the smooth edge. “Sunday afternoon,” he says. “If the wood is dry, we can do the blue end.”

Ronan looks at him carefully.

“You have time?”

“I kept that afternoon free. Your mum has the table until two.”

Mum nods. “And I want it covered.”

Ronan puts the old paper beside the boat so it will be ready. Then he leaves it alone. Dad's work shirt hangs from its new peg. Mum will clear the table by two on Sunday. After that, Ronan and Dad will paint the boat. He can wait two more days for the paint.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- regular＝固定的、规律的
- pay＝工资
- peg＝挂钩
- kept that afternoon free＝留出了那个下午

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：elbow＝手肘位置；patch＝补丁；tear＝裂口。

## 读句提示

**Where can I put this peg?**

我能／把这枚挂钩安在／哪里？把asked where从句展开成Dad的原话。

## 理解问题

1. Dad的工作比之前稳定在哪里？
2. 家人怎样安排彼此的工作与木船上色？
